name: Greece

chips.label: Earned prosperity
chips.why: Institutions roughly match or exceed what income predicts - durable.
chips.rule: MI residual vs. the log-GDP regression (the durability gap): below -0.03 → granted, otherwise earned (a ±0.03 tolerance treats near-zero gaps as in-line).

chips.label: Lopsided · weakest: Economic Complexity
chips.why: Spread between the strongest and weakest pillar - the country's structural shape.

verdict: Structurally durable - prosperity roughly in line with institutions - lopsided (economic complexity the weak point).

checks.title: Durability gate
checks.headline: income vs institutions +0.21
checks.detail: Income runs somewhat ahead of institutions - a gap worth watching, though not yet a clear warning.

checks.title: Weakest link
checks.headline: Economic Complexity is lowest
checks.detail: Economic Complexity is the pillar dragging the score down. A chain breaks at its weakest link, so this is where the structural risk concentrates.

checks.title: Room to rise
checks.headline: already high
checks.detail: The base is already high, so large structural jumps from here are historically rare.

relational.label: Greece, Asia Minor campaign 1919-1922 (engine-alone MISS — EXOGENOUS-military)
relational.joint_reading: HIGH structural exposure + NO patron + weak response: standing vulnerability to externally-imposed shock that the internal MI does not see. If a shock lands, little absorbs it. This is the configuration that turns an internal 'OK' read into an external miss - Cyprus 1974, Poland-Lithuania 1772.
relational.outcome_factual: Catastrophic defeat in Anatolia (1922); Smyrna burned; population exchange; the 1922 revolution at home.
